question: What is the primary goal of triage during a community-based obstetric emergency?

options.A: Complete detailed family health background records
options.B: Quickly identify life-threatening complications requiring urgent care
options.C: Perform a comprehensive physical head-to-toe assessment
options.D: Determine the exact gestational age of the fetus

explanation: Triage prioritizes rapid identification of critical danger signs so immediate life-saving interventions can begin without delay. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h1)

question: A patient presents to a rural clinic with severe postpartum bleeding. What makes immediate assessment vital in this low-resource setting?

options.A: Complications can rapidly escalate to maternal death
options.B: Patients refuse treatment if delayed past ten minutes
options.C: National health insurance mandates immediate chart closure
options.D: Laboratory equipment requires calibration every hour

explanation: Obstetric emergencies like hemorrhage deteriorate very quickly, making prompt recognition essential to prevent mortality. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is keeping a postpartum hemorrhage patient warm important in the community?

options.D: Warmth stimulates rapid breast milk production

explanation: Cold temperatures impair the clotting cascade, which increases the severity of bleeding in postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h2)

question: Which position should a healthcare worker use for a pregnant woman experiencing umbilical cord prolapse in the community?

options.B: Flat supine position with legs fully extended
options.C: Upright sitting position in a cushioned chair
options.D: Prone position flat on her stomach

explanation: The knee-chest or Trendelenburg position uses gravity to shift the fetus off the umbilical cord, preserving oxygen flow. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the most common underlying cause of severe postpartum hemorrhage?
explanation: Failure of the uterus to contract properly after delivery accounts for the vast majority of postpartum bleeding cases. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h3)

question: A community midwife gives oxytocin and massages the uterus, but bleeding continues and the bladder is distended. What is the next immediate nursing action?

options.A: Perform a routine abdominal ultrasound scan
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk around the room
options.C: Insert a urinary catheter to empty the bladder

explanation: A distended bladder displaces the uterus and prevents effective contractions, so emptying it is critical to stop bleeding. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h3)

question: What is the drug of choice for treating and preventing seizures in severe preeclampsia and eclampsia?
explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the internationally recognized medication for controlling eclamptic seizures and protecting the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why is placing an eclamptic patient in the lateral position essential during a seizure?

options.A: It lowers the core body temperature safely
options.B: It makes intravenous cannula insertion easier
options.C: It stops the muscular contractions instantly
options.D: It prevents aspiration of oral secretions and vomit

explanation: Turning the patient on her side keeps the airway clear and prevents saliva or vomit from entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why is giving uterotonic drugs dangerous when managing obstructed labor in a community setting?

options.A: It permanently stops all future menstrual cycles
options.B: It can cause the muscular wall of the uterus to rupture
options.C: It accelerates fetal growth beyond pelvic capacity
options.D: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in newborns

explanation: Stimulating contractions against a mechanical blockage forces the uterine muscle to tear, endangering both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h5)

question: What clinical tool is used in primary clinics to monitor the progress of labor and spot prolonged stages early?
explanation: The partograph provides a pictorial overview of labor progress, alerting birth attendants to abnormal delays. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h5)

question: What crucial document must accompany an emergency obstetric patient being transferred from a community clinic to a hospital?

options.B: A written referral note with clinical details

explanation: A formal referral note ensures receiving clinicians know what treatment has already been given and what the primary diagnosis is. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h6)

question: Which factor contributes most to the second delay in managing rural obstetric emergencies?

options.B: Inadequate transportation and poor road infrastructure
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced surgical theaters
options.D: Refusal of doctors to examine emergency patients

explanation: The second delay refers to the time and difficulty involved in physically moving a patient from the community to a referral facility. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h6)
